orientation.batter_faces: Northeast. Home plate sits in the southwest of the bowl and the batter looks out toward center field to the northeast. Consequence: the third-base/left-field side is the shade side; the first-base side and right field are the sunny side. Sun sets behind the third-base stands near the left-field foul pole.

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE toward first base and right field. Walking the bowl in order of ascending number you go: left-field foul pole -> third-base line -> behind home plate -> first-base line -> right-field foul pole -> right field -> center field -> left field. Every level follows the same rotational direction. Lower numbers = third base / left field; higher numbers = first base / right field. On the 200 level the numbering keeps going past the right-field foul pole through the outfield and finishes in left field (257-260), so the highest 200-level numbers are back on the LEFT-field side - the only place the 'higher = right field' shorthand breaks.

accessibility.summary: 'Over 500 wheelchair, semi-ambulatory, and companion tickets are available throughout the ballpark.' Three designated ticket categories exist at Angel Stadium: Wheelchair, Semi-Ambulatory, and Companion. 'Individuals purchasing a ticket for an accessible seat may purchase up to three (3) additional seats for their companions in the same row and that are contiguous with the accessible seat.' Accessible seating is offered at all price levels. Purchase by phone at (714) 4-ANGELS or at the ticket windows near the Home Plate Gate. Elevators and escalators throughout the stadium reach all levels, with priority given to guests with special needs. Accessible parking is in the lots surrounding Gates 1-6 and at the Home Plate Gate. Complimentary wheelchair escort assistance runs from the gates to ticketed seats, but wheelchairs cannot be checked out for personal use. Service animals are welcome; emotional-support animals are not. Assistive listening devices are available from Guest Relations at Section 133.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE LETTERS at every level of Angel Stadium - there are no numbered rows. Field Level (100s) rows run AA, BB, then A-Z (Row A/AA nearest the field, entrance at Row Z at the back); note 'I', 'O' and 'Q' are skipped in the A-Z runs (sequences observed go ...H, J, K, L... and ...N, P, R, S...). Lexus Diamond Club section 118 runs C-W plus a table row labelled 'TBL'. Terrace Level (200s) rows run A-L with the entrance at Row L. Pavilion sections use A-Z plus double-letter rows at the back (e.g. section 240: A-Z then VV, WW, XX, YY; section 258: G-Z plus a 'WC' wheelchair row). Club Level (300s) rows run A-H, entrance at Row H. View 400 Level rows run A-J, entrance at Row J. View 500 Level rows run A-R, entrance at Row A (at the front, because you climb up into the section from below); 'Rows D and above are under cover.' SEATS are numbers, starting at 1, and row width grows toward the back of the section (e.g. section 101 Row AA has 9 seats, Row Z has 21).
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the left" - stated on rateyourseats.com section pages, e.g. https://www.rateyourseats.com/angel-stadium/seating/sections/419 , https://www.rateyourseats.com/angel-stadium/seating/sections/521 , https://www.rateyourseats.com/angel-stadium/seating/sections/321 . The Field Level pages render it as "When looking towards the field/field, lower number seats are on the left" (e.g. sections 101, 106, 130, 135). So seat 1 is on the LEFT as you face the field, and seat numbers increase to the right.
discovery.known_obstructions: 1) Section 135 (right-field corner, Field Level): 'The Right Field Pavilion blocks your view of Left Field and Center Field in section 135.' 2) Right Field Pavilion sections (241-249): 'the main scoreboard sits above these sections, meaning fans seated here will not have a clear view of it' - the main videoboard is in right field, directly overhead. 3) Section 436 (last section of the 400 Level, right-field corner): the yellow foul pole blocks the first-base line, and right-field visibility is obstructed by 'chain-link fence, railing and whole section of fans'; Row J also gets air-conditioning and freeway noise. 4) 400/500 Level corner sections generally have railing/fence interference at the low rows. 5) Terrace Level sections are fully under the overhang - great shade, but the overhang cuts off high fly balls and the upper scoreboard from the back rows. 6) Field Level is uncovered, so sun (not obstruction) is the main complaint; the first-base side and right field are the sunny side.
